title: Who's responsible
idea: Every transmission has a control operator. The station licensee picks that person, and when it's someone else, both share the blame.

items: Control operator is not the licensee
A repeater passes on a violation
The originating station's control operator is accountable
Recommended by a volunteer frequency coordinator, chosen by local hams

pairs: Keeps people under RF exposure limits
Sets which frequencies you can use
Responsible when a friend operates your station
Accountable when a repeater relays a violation
Local hams who could run repeaters
Any ham allowed on the uplink

compare.how: Holds the station license. Names the control operator. Answers for RF exposure.
The person designated to be responsible for transmissions. Their license class sets the privileges.
Where the control operator function is performed.

traps.wrong: When using automatic control, such as in the case of a repeater
traps.why: Even a repeater has a control operator. A station never transmits without one.

traps.wrong: The highest class of operator license held by anyone on the premises
traps.why: It's the control operator's license class that counts, not whoever is in the room.

traps.wrong: When designated as the control operator by an Amateur Extra Class licensee
traps.why: Outside an emergency, a Technician can never control a station in an Extra-only segment.
When someone else is the control operator, both the control operator and the licensee are responsible.

traps.wrong: The control operator of the repeater
traps.why: The originating station's control operator is accountable, not the repeater's.
The station licensee makes sure no one is exposed above the limits.

traps.wrong: A Frequency Spectrum Manager appointed by the FCC
traps.why: The FCC isn't involved. A volunteer frequency coordinator recognized by local hams recommends channels.

traps.wrong: Only an Amateur Extra Class operator
traps.why: Any ham allowed to transmit on the satellite's uplink frequency can be the control operator.
